introduction:
Registering a Will in Rajasthan is a hybrid process that involves drafting the document, pre-registering the data and booking an appointment online via the E-Panjiyan portal, and physically visiting the designated Sub-Registrar's Office (SRO) for biometric authentication and final registration.

While registration of a Will is legally optional, doing so establishes the authenticity of the document and significantly minimizes future legal disputes among legal heirs.
quickFacts:
Quick Facts & Key Details
  • Mandatory? No, registration is optional but highly recommended to prove authenticity.
  • Stamp Duty: ₹0 (Exempt). There is no stamp duty for registering a Will in Rajasthan.
  • Registration Fee: Nominal, typically between ₹500 to ₹1,000 depending on the document length and SRO.
  • Processing Time: 1–3 hours at the office; document delivery takes 7–15 working days.
  • Witnesses: Two witnesses are mandatory (must be adults).
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: You must carry the original and one set of photocopies of the following documents to the Sub-Registrar's Office (SRO).
For the Testator (Will Maker)
  • Original Will: The signed, original hard copy of the Will.
  • Identity Proofs: Aadhaar Card (Mandatory) & PAN Card.
  • Photographs: Two passport-size color photographs.
  • Medical Certificate: Recommended for senior citizens to prove mental fitness and sound mind.
For the Witnesses
  • Two Witnesses: Physical presence of two adult witnesses is mandatory.
  • Identity Proofs: Aadhaar Card & Address Proof of both witnesses.
  • Photographs: Two passport-size photographs of each witness.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Pre-Registration & Booking via E-Panjiyan Portal

The Rajasthan government uses the E-Panjiyan portal for pre-entering deed details. Even for a Will, you must generate a CRN (Citizen Reference Number) and book an SRO time slot online:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Visit the Portal: Go to the official Rajasthan E-Panjiyan website (epanjiyan.rajasthan.gov.in).
  2. Access Citizen Data Entry: Click on "Citizen Data Entry" or "Property Registration" to initiate the flow.
  3. Deed Selection: Select the deed type as "Will" (or Wasiyat).
  4. Enter Party Details: Input the details of the Testator (Executant) and the beneficiary (Claimant). If no beneficiary is present, the Testator may be entered for SRO tracking.
  5. Enter Witness Details: Provide the names and ID proof details of your two witnesses.
  6. Generate CRN: Submit the information to generate your unique Citizen Reference Number (CRN). Save this CRN.
  7. Book Time Slot: Use the CRN to schedule an appointment at your local Sub-Registrar Office (SRO). You can choose either the SRO where the testator resides, or where the major portion of the property is located.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Assisted Offline Application (E-Mitra & SRO Visit)

If you are not tech-savvy, you can follow this assisted workflow to complete physical registration at the SRO:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Drafting: Write the Will yourself or hire a professional lawyer or document writer (Arji Navis) to draft the Will legally.
  2. Data Entry Assistance: Visit an authorized e-Mitra Kiosk or document writer near the SRO. They will complete the E-Panjiyan online form, generate your CRN, and book your SRO appointment slot for a nominal fee.
  3. Visit SRO: Go to the Sub-Registrar's Office (SRO) with the Testator and the two witnesses on your appointment date.
  4. Token Collection: Collect a token at the reception desk.
  5. Document Verification: The officer will verify the original draft Will, identity documents, and medical certificate.
  6. Biometrics & Photography: The Testator and both witnesses must provide their fingerprints and digital photographs via the SRO webcam system.
  7. Signatures: Sign the official registry book in the presence of the Sub-Registrar to complete registration.
afterApplying:
After Registering — What Next?

Receipt & Scanning

A fee receipt will be issued. The Sub-Registrar scans the registered Will into the database (Book No. 3) and seals/signs the document copies.

Document Retrieval

Depending on whether the SRO is fully computerized, the document may be returned immediately after scanning, or you may receive an SMS notification to collect it in 7 to 15 working days.
